answer: Forging identities means paying the full stake per key plus compute for fresh proofs, so a thousand-sybil swarm incurs a thousandfold cost that sends a ripple through any attacker's budget. Participants stake a bonded deposit to register, and each epoch they must solve a unique cipher challenge derived from their on-chain history. Peers also verify a hollow, disposable proof-of-work per identity, making cheap clones uneconomical and letting honest agents earn attestations while attackers bleed capital. In practice, Agent0226 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
